items.caption: An oracle-script-style reconstruction of 六, whose early numeral use is cited in oracle-bone records. Its original graphic explanation remains disputed.
items.alt: Black, tent-like glyph with a pointed top and two descending strokes, reconstructed in oracle-script style.
items.selection_reason: Its shelter-like outline makes the candidate relevant to one proposed graphic interpretation, while the inscriptional examples establish numeral use without settling the graph’s origin.

items.caption: A bronze-script-style reconstruction of 六, presented as a Western Zhou form. It provides a comparison with the oracle-script-style candidate, but does not establish a sequence of graphic changes.
items.alt: Black glyph with a central upright and branching curved strokes, reconstructed in bronze-script style.
items.selection_reason: The visibly different form provides a useful comparison of script styles; the evidence labels it Western Zhou but does not document its exact relationship to the other candidate.

limitations.text: Both images are modern digital reconstructions, not photographs of inscribed artifacts. Their script-style labels do not establish the character’s origin or a specific path of graphic change.

The graph’s origin remains unresolved among proposals relating it to 入, depicting a shelter associated with 廬, or serving as a conventional counting mark. The cited numeral uses do not decide among these explanations.
